prompt: Complete LineNumberer.numberLines so it reads every line from a BufferedReader and returns them numbered like "1: first\n2: second" with no trailing newline.
explanation: BufferedReader.readLine() strips the line terminator and returns null at end of stream, so the standard pattern is while ((line = in.readLine()) != null). Appending the separator BEFORE every line except the first is the easy way to join pieces without a trailing newline. A StringBuilder avoids creating a new String on every concatenation inside the loop.
hints: Loop with while ((line = in.readLine()) != null) and keep a counter starting at 1.
Build the result in a StringBuilder: number, then ": ", then the line text.
Append "\n" only before the second and later lines -- that leaves no trailing newline.
